definition: The Naglieri Nonverbal Ability Test is a nonverbal assessment used to measure cognitive ability without relying on language. In the source, it appears as a comparison measure for evaluating another nonverbal intelligence test.

reasons: The packet supports that the Naglieri Nonverbal Ability Test–I (NNAT-I) was used as a comparison measure in criterion-related validity analyses, but it does not define the test itself as a nonverbal assessment for measuring cognitive ability without language reliance.

The definition adds a general description of the test’s purpose and format that is not stated for the NNAT-I in the packet; the packet only gives a general background description of nonverbal intelligence tests, not this named instrument specifically.

The packet does not support the claim that the Naglieri Nonverbal Ability Test “measure[s] cognitive ability without relying on language.” It only refers to the test as a criterion-related validity measure (NNAT-I) used for correlations.
The packet does not state that it is “used to measure cognitive ability” in general terms; it only indicates it was used to evaluate criterion-related validity alongside TONI-3.

While the packet does support that NNAT-I was used as a comparison/validity measure (criterion-related validity) in the study context, the definition also contains unsupported descriptive claims about what the test measures and how (language reliance).
